chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ibrahim ibn Muslim, from Abu Shibl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The believer, when he shaves his head in Mina, then buries it, will come on the Day of Resurrection, and every hair will have a tongue, eloquently reciting the Talbiyah in the name of its owner.

key_terms.تُلَبِّي: Reciting the Talbiyah (the Hajj invocation: 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk').
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a sacred site near Mecca where pilgrims perform specific rituals.

ai.seo_question: What happens to the shaved hair of a believer during Hajj on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi highlights the concept of 'shahid al-sha'r' (hair as witness), where the physical act of shaving during Hajj becomes a permanent, vocal testimony of devotion. Scholars interpret the 'tongue' of each hair as a miraculous sign that validates the believer's intent and ritual purity, linking the mundane act of grooming to eternal accountability. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the spiritual weight of minor acts of worship when performed with sincerity.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Ibrahim Bin Muslim, from Abu Shibl, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Believer, when he shaves off his head in Mina, then buries it, would come on the Day of Judgement, and every hair would have a tongue for it exclaiming Talbiyya in the name of its owner’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan from Ibrahim ibn Muslim from abu Shibl who has said the following: “

When a believing person shaves his head and buries his hairs in Mina, on the Day of Judgment every hair comes with a clear tongue, saying Talbiyah (here I am, O Lord, to obey Your command) for the one to whom they belonged.”
